findings.evidence: Lines 396-400: `rw [pathLink_staplePath_ofBilin, ofBilin_apply, ← Circle.exp_add] at h` followed by `have hphase : B (0 + (0, 1)) (0 - (0, 1)) / 2 + -(((B - B.flip) (1, 0) (0, 1) + ... ) / 2) = -1` and `rw [hphase] at h`.
findings.fix: Assert the value instead of the phase, e.g. `have : (ofBilin B).pathLink (staplePath (1,0) (0,1) 0 (0,1)) = Circle.exp (-1 : ℝ) := by rw [pathLink_staplePath_ofBilin, ofBilin_apply, ← Circle.exp_add]; congr 1; simp [hB]`, then derive the contradiction from that; the statement then no longer depends on how the RHS of `pathLink_staplePath_ofBilin` is parenthesised.
findings.issue: `hphase` restates, verbatim across three lines, the exact phase subterm produced by `pathLink_staplePath_ofBilin` + `ofBilin_apply` + `Circle.exp_add`, purely so `rw [hphase] at h` matches syntactically. Any reassociation of the author's own flux formula on line 378 silently breaks this proof and forces re-transcription.

findings.evidence: Lines 287-289: `rw [staplePath_def, pathLink_smul]` then `rw [List.getLast_cons_cons, List.getLast_cons_cons, List.getLast_cons_cons, List.getLast_singleton]`.
findings.fix: Replace the second `rw` with one `simp only [List.getLast_cons_cons, List.getLast_singleton]` (or factor a reusable `staplePath_getLast : (staplePath v w x y).getLast h = y`, which any other `pathLink_smul`-on-a-staple result will need too).
findings.issue: `pathLink_staplePath_smul` finishes with a chain of four sequential named rewrites (`List.getLast_cons_cons` three times, then `List.getLast_singleton`) to evaluate `getLast` on a four-element literal list — exactly the rewrite chain that breaks on an upstream rename and that also has to be relengthened if `staplePath` ever gains a corner.

summary: Proofs are mostly short and well-automated (group, module, ring, simp) with no change/show and no undocumented defeq across wrappers. Two spots are needlessly brittle: a verbatim transcription of a long phase expression used only to drive a rewrite, and a four-step chain of List.getLast rewrites.
